editorial.headline: Commodity Futures Investment Management: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers pooled-fund management for commodity futures contracts, with national foreign ownership open to 100% and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Commodity futures investment management is the business of gathering and managing money from individuals or groups of individuals for investment in futures contracts. Its scope also includes parties acting as representative managers of a futures fund centre. In practical terms, the activity is defined by the stewardship of pooled investment funds directed into commodity futures—not simply by an interest in the market itself.

The registration field is available across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the record does not confine the activity to one size of operator. It recognises a continuum from micro through large-scale enterprise, while keeping the central identity of the activity constant: collecting and managing investor funds for futures-contract investment. The scope also specifically names the representative-manager function, while distinguishing the wider activity group from that role.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. At the national level, this activity remains TERBUKA and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. That means foreign participation is fully open at the national level; there is no lower foreign-equity cap stated in this record. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders assessing structure, the useful conclusion is precise: the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity, rather than presenting a partial-access arrangement.

Bali does not reverse that national position. The provincial record marks the activity as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and confirms that it is not blocked by the moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—medium-high/high—which is why the moratorium does not apply. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA restriction covers Low and Medium-Low risk activities; this activity sits outside that blocked category on the stated risk basis. There is no Bali-specific foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition recorded here, so none should be inferred. The honest reading is therefore clear: foreign ownership can reach 100% nationally, and PMA registration for this activity is not blocked in Bali by the recorded moratorium.
